record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Yang [803] claims to prove the following: let P (z), Q(z) be monic poly- nomials such that (i) P (z) = 0 ⇐⇒ Q(z) = 0, and (ii) P ′ (z) = 0 ⇐⇒ Q′ (z) = 0. Then there exist positive integers m, n such that P (z)m ≡ Q(z)n . As pointed out by Rubinstein (personal communication), Yang’s proof is incorrect since the inequalities [803, p. 597] are wrong. The problem then is to settle the Yang conjecture. If we let {z1 , z2 , . . . , zν } be the distinct points at which P (and therefore Q) has zeros, then the conjecture is easily established if ν ≤ 5, and also in the case that ν is arbitrary and all the points zi are collinear. (E. B. Saff )

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P(z)$ and $Q(z)$ be monic polynomials in the complex variable $z$ satisfying:
(i) $P(z) = 0 \iff Q(z) = 0$ (i.e., $P$ and $Q$ have the same set of zeros, ignoring multiplicities), and
(ii) $P'(z) = 0 \iff Q'(z) = 0$ (i.e., $P$ and $Q$ have the same set of critical points, ignoring multiplicities).

Prove or disprove: there exist positive integers $m$ and $n$ such that
$$P(z)^m \equiv Q(z)^n.$$

It is known that the statement holds when the number $\nu$ of distinct zeros of $P$ satisfies $\nu \le 5$, and also when $\nu$ is arbitrary but all the distinct zeros are collinear. The general case (arbitrary $\nu$, arbitrary configuration of distinct zeros in $\mathbb{C}$) is the question to be settled.
artifact.category_tag: Zeros and critical points of polynomials
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of Yang's conjecture on polynomials sharing zero sets and critical-point sets. The conjecture is recorded as still requiring settlement (after Yang's original proof was found to be flawed), with only the cases of at most five distinct zeros and the collinear case being established. No published proof or counterexample for the general case was located in the search.
